title: Sprint 2, task 1: How good is AskMate?
where: Every real AI product is measured with a set of test questions. From now on, you can prove AskMate got better, in numbers.
next: Go back to the portal. Your checks are running.

steps.title: The owner asks: how good is it?
steps.body:
HomeShine's owner tried AskMate and liked it. Then she asked: "How often is it right? And does it ever answer wrongly with confidence?"
Saying "it works" is not an answer. Engineers answer with a test set: questions where the right answer is known, asked again after every change.
This task also brings a new answer.py and main.py. You do not need to change them: each task in this sprint adds one small file, and AskMate uses it as soon as it exists.

steps.title: Look at the test questions
steps.body: Open data/gold.json. Each test question says what AskMate should do: answer with a product, ask which one, or refuse (an honest no).
steps.prompt: How many test questions are there?
steps.retry: Count the lines that start with {"q". The file is short: scroll to the end.

steps.title: Is this reply right?
steps.body: The problem. To count right answers, AskMate needs a rule for what right means.
steps.ask: Make is_right say True when AskMate decided what the test question wants.
steps.gets: AskMate's reply, like {"action": "answer", "products": ["OPC 186"]}, and the test question's wish, like {"action": "answer", "products": ["OPC 186"]}
approach: Right needs two things at once: the same action, and every wanted product named.
For the products, a set helps: set(want["products"]) <= set(reply["products"]) is True when every wanted product is in the reply.
steps.done: every row of the Try it table is green.
hints: Look at the table's false rows. Which of the two things is wrong in each?
Two comparisons joined with and. For products, <= between two sets means "all of these are in that".
Nearly there:  return reply["action"] == want["action"] and set(want["products"]) <= set(____["products"])

answer.why: The action must match, and every wanted product must be in the reply. For a which-one question, AskMate may name more products than the test lists, so we check that the wanted ones are among them, not that the lists are equal.

steps.well_done: Now AskMate's answers can be marked right or wrong.

cases.show: ask OPC 186 + 2 more, wants answer OPC 186
ask 3 basins, wants ask 2 of them

steps.title: Three numbers for the owner
steps.body: The problem. A long list of right and wrong is hard to read. The owner wants three numbers.
steps.ask: Make scorecard turn the list of results into three numbers.
steps.gets: a list of results. Each one is {"want": ..., "reply": ..., "right": True or False}
approach: right_percent: count the results whose right is True, divide by how many there are, times 100, rounded with round().
honest_no_percent: take only the results whose want action is refuse. Of those, what percent did AskMate really refuse? If there are none, use 100.
confident_mistakes: count the results where AskMate's reply action is answer, but it was not right. This is the worst mistake: a wrong answer said with confidence.
Return the three in a dictionary with exactly these keys.
steps.done: every row of the Try it table is green.
hints: Do one number at a time, and check the table after each save.
sum(1 for r in results if r["right"]) counts the right ones. A list comprehension picks the refuse ones: [r for r in results if r["want"]["action"] == "refuse"].
Nearly there:  mistakes = sum(1 for r in results if r["reply"]["action"] == "answer" and not r["____"])

answer.why: Each number counts something different. Right percent is the overall grade. Honest no checks AskMate never pretends to sell what HomeShine does not. Confident mistakes counts the most harmful error: a wrong answer the customer believes.

cases.show: 4 results: 3 right, a refuse that was answered

steps.title: Measure AskMate
steps.body:
Type the command below in your second terminal. It asks AskMate all 30 test questions and prints your three numbers, then every question it missed.
Write your three numbers down: you compare them after every task from now on. Then add 3 test questions of your own to the end of data/gold.json, from your Friend Test in Sprint 1. Keep the same shape, and the commas between them.

steps.title: Commit your change
steps.body: Type these in your second terminal:
steps.cmd:
git add .
git commit -m "Measure AskMate with a test set"

steps.title: Send it to GitHub
steps.body: Push, and your checks start on GitHub.
